title: Processing of identified access code data
description: The guest's temporary access code is processed by the Home Hub, which may be linked to the guest's identity through system logs or other data sources.
assumptions: The system maintains logs of access codes and may associate them with guest identity.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system logs access codes and can associate them with guest identity.

title: Revealing attributes through access attempt
description: The act of entering an access code reveals that the guest is attempting to access the home, which is a revealing attribute about the guest's presence and intent.
assumptions: The system records the attempt regardless of success.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system records all access attempts.

title: Sensitive access code data collection
description: The access code is sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than functionally required for simple door unlocking.
assumptions: The access code could be considered sensitive personal data.
uncertainty_note: Assuming access codes are treated as sensitive personal data under privacy frameworks.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: The Home Hub may analyze or store the access code beyond what is needed for the immediate door unlocking function.
assumptions: The system may log, store, or analyze access codes for future reference or analytics.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system may retain access codes beyond immediate use.

title: Guest unawareness of data processing
description: The guest may not be aware that their access code and access attempt data is being collected, stored, or processed by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: The guest may not receive clear notification about data collection practices.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the guest may not be fully informed about data practices.

title: Lack of guest control over data preferences
description: The guest may not have control over how their access data is processed, stored, or shared by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: The system may not provide options for the guest to control data processing preferences.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system may not offer data control options to guests.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data (access codes, access attempts) than is actually needed for the functional goal of door unlocking.
assumptions: The system may collect and store more data than strictly necessary for door access functionality.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system may not adhere strictly to data minimization principles.

title: Linking through unique identifier in video metadata
description: Video clips uploaded from Home Hub may contain metadata with unique identifiers (device ID, user account, timestamp, location) that can be used to link data to specific individuals or devices.
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination in video content
description: Video footage may contain multiple quasi-identifiers (time, location, visual attributes) that when combined can uniquely identify individuals even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Video content contains observable attributes that can be combined for identification

title: Processing of identified data in video clips
description: Video clips may contain identified information (faces, license plates, recognizable locations) that directly identifies data subjects.
assumptions: Video content captures identifiable individuals or objects

title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert
description: The real-time motion alert may contain device identifiers or user identifiers that could be used to link the motion event to a specific individual or device.
assumptions: Motion alerts typically include device or user identification for routing and attribution purposes.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion alert data combined with other available data (e.g., location, time, device type) could serve as quasi-identifiers to link to specific individuals.
assumptions: Motion data is often contextualized with metadata that can be combined for identification purposes.

title: Processing of identified data in motion alert
description: The motion alert may contain or be associated with identified information about the user or device owner.
assumptions: Real-time alerts are typically tied to specific users/devices for notification purposes.

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion alert data may reveal attributes about the data subject such as presence, activity patterns, or location that support identification.
assumptions: Motion data inherently reveals behavioral and contextual information about the user.

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data may be more sensitive than needed
description: Motion data could be perceived as highly sensitive (revealing presence, activity patterns) and may be collected/processed beyond what is strictly required for the alert functionality.
assumptions: Motion alerts are often part of broader security or monitoring systems that collect more data than the immediate alert requires.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Motion alert data may be propagated to other services or systems where it is not functionally needed for the alert purpose.
assumptions: Data flows in IoT ecosystems often involve multiple downstream services that may not all require the motion data.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Real-time alerts are often triggered automatically without explicit user consent for each transmission.

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed and shared.
assumptions: Motion alert systems often operate with default settings that users may not actively configure.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (motion data) may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of sending a real-time alert.
assumptions: Motion data collection may be broader than the minimum required to trigger and deliver an alert.

title: Linking through unique identifier in notification
description: The motion-detected notification likely contains the homeowner's unique identifier (e.g., user ID, phone number) to route the notification to the correct recipient, enabling linking of the notification to a specific individual.
assumptions: The notification includes identifying information to deliver to the correct homeowner.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Motion detection data may include location, time, and device information that can be combined to create a quasi-identifier, potentially linking the notification to a specific homeowner's habits and location patterns.
assumptions: Motion data includes location/time attributes that can be combined.

title: Processing of identified data for notification delivery
description: The system processes identified homeowner data to deliver motion-detected notifications, requiring the homeowner's identity to be known and processed.
assumptions: Homeowner identity is required to deliver notifications.

title: Revealing attributes through motion detection
description: Motion detection data reveals revealing attributes such as time of day, location, and activity patterns of the homeowner, which can support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion data includes time and location information.

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The notification itself serves as an observed communication that reveals motion was detected at a specific time and location, potentially exposing the homeowner's presence or absence.
assumptions: Notification delivery reveals motion detection event.

title: Excessive data type granularity in notification
description: The notification may include more granular location or time data than functionally necessary for simply alerting the homeowner about motion detection.
assumptions: Notification includes precise location/time beyond what's needed for alert.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: Motion detection data may be analyzed, enriched, or processed beyond what is functionally needed to simply send a notification to the homeowner.
assumptions: Motion data undergoes additional processing beyond notification delivery.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware that motion detection data is being collected, processed, and transmitted to their device beyond the notification itself.
assumptions: Homeowner may not understand full scope of motion data processing.

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: The homeowner may have limited control over how motion detection data is processed, stored, or shared beyond basic notification preferences.
assumptions: Limited user control over motion data processing settings.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Motion detection data may be processed beyond what is strictly necessary for the functional goal of sending a notification, potentially violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds functional necessity for notification.
